title: Design Video Sharing Platform
statement:
Build a class `VideoSharingPlatform` that hosts videos. A video is a string of digits, and its character at index `i` is what the video shows at minute `i`. Every hosted video has an integer id and keeps its own counts of views, likes and dislikes, which all start at 0.

- `VideoSharingPlatform()` starts with no videos.
- `upload(video)` hosts `video` under the smallest non-negative integer that is not the id of a currently hosted video, and returns that id. So the id of a removed video can be handed out again, and the new video under it starts with fresh counts.
- `remove(videoId)` deletes the video hosted under `videoId`; if there is none, nothing happens.
- `watch(videoId, startMinute, endMinute)`: if a video is hosted under `videoId`, add one view to it and return its characters from index `startMinute` through index `min(endMinute, video.length - 1)`, both ends included. If there is no such video, return `"-1"`.
- `like(videoId)` and `dislike(videoId)` add one like or one dislike to the video hosted under `videoId`; if there is none, nothing happens.
- `getLikesAndDislikes(videoId)` returns `[likes, dislikes]` for the video hosted under `videoId`, or `[-1]` if there is none.
- `getViews(videoId)` returns the view count of the video hosted under `videoId`, or `-1` if there is none.
constraints: The uploaded videos have at most 10^5 digits in total
When a video is hosted under videoId, startMinute < video.length for that video
The sum of endMinute - startMinute over all watch calls is at most 10^5
At most 10^5 calls are made in total

signature.name: VideoSharingPlatform
methods: String watch(int videoId, int startMinute, int endMinute)

notes:
## Intuition

Most of the work is bookkeeping: each hosted id needs its string and three counters, which a hash map from id to a small record gives in O(1). The one real question is which id `upload` hands out. It must be the smallest id not in use. Every id below `nextId` has been used before, so the candidates are the ids that were freed by `remove`, and `nextId` itself when none are free. Scanning upwards from 0 for a gap works but costs O(n) per upload. Keeping the freed ids in a min-heap returns the smallest one in O(log n).

## Approach

1. Keep `videos`, a map from id to `{ content, views, likes, dislikes }`, the counter `nextId` of never-used ids, and `freeIds`, a min-heap of freed ids.
2. `upload`: take the smallest freed id if there is one, otherwise `nextId` (and advance it). Store a fresh record under it and return it.
3. `remove`: delete the id from `videos`; only if something was actually deleted, push the id onto the heap.
4. `watch`: return `"-1"` for a missing id. Otherwise add a view, clip the last minute to `content.length - 1` and return that slice.
5. `like`, `dislike`, `getLikesAndDislikes` and `getViews` look up the record and update or report it, with `-1` or `[-1]` for a missing id.
6. `addFreeId` and `takeSmallestFreeId` are the usual sift-up and sift-down of a binary heap.

## Example 1, step by step

- `upload("123")` gets id 0, `upload("456")` gets id 1.
- `remove(4)` deletes nothing, so 4 is not added to `freeIds`. `remove(0)` deletes video 0 and pushes 0.
- `upload("789")` pops 0 from `freeIds` and returns 0.
- `watch(1, 0, 5)`: `lastMinute = min(5, 2) = 2`, so it returns `"456"`; `watch(1, 0, 1)` returns `"45"`. Video 1 now has 2 views.
- One like and two dislikes give `[1, 2]`, and `getViews(1)` is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n) for `upload` and `remove` (heap operations), O(1) for the counters, and O(endMinute - startMinute) for `watch` to build the slice.
- Space: O(total length of the hosted videos + number of ids).

## Pitfalls

- Only push an id when `remove` really deleted a video; otherwise an unused id, or one removed twice, could be handed out twice.
- A reused id belongs to a new video, so its views, likes and dislikes start from 0.
- Clip `endMinute` to the last index; it may run past the end of the video.
- `watch` returns the string `"-1"` and `getLikesAndDislikes` returns `[-1]`, not the number `-1`. Return the slice as a string so leading zeros survive.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `videos` | map from hosted id to its record |
| `entry` | the record `{ content, views, likes, dislikes }` of one video |
| `nextId` | smallest id that has never been handed out |
| `freeIds` | min-heap of ids freed by `remove` |
| `lastMinute` | last index `watch` returns, after clipping |
| `heap`, `index`, `parent`, `child` | the heap array and positions while sifting |
